{
  "analysis": "The training data reveals that German legal texts contain person entities in two primary contexts: judges/lawyers (often preceded by titles like Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., Hon.-Prof.) and parties in the case (preceded by role indicators like 'klagenden Partei', 'beklagte Partei', 'gegen', 'Antragsteller'). The main challenge is distinguishing between titles and names, and capturing full names that may include multiple parts or suffixes like 'MBA'.",
  "strategy": "Use two focused regex rules: one for titles followed by names (judges/lawyers) and one for names following legal role indicators (parties), ensuring capture groups isolate the name text for accurate start/end offsets.",
  "note": "Every rule includes output_template and output_key. Patterns use capture groups to extract only the name, avoiding inclusion of surrounding context words.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "title_person",
      "description": "Matches person names preceded by academic or professional titles (Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., Hon.-Prof., PhD, etc.)",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Dr\\.|Mag\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.|Hon\\.-Prof\\.|PhD|Vizepr\\.|Senatspr\\.|Hofrat|Hofr\\u00e4t|Prof\\.?)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+MBA)?(?:\\s+und\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)?)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 9,
      "reasoning": "Covers judges and lawyers with titles. The pattern handles multiple name parts, MBA suffixes, and the 'und' conjunction seen in training data (e.g., 'MMag. Sloboda und Dr. Kikinger' is split into two entities by the regex engine as it matches sequentially)."
    },
    {
      "name": "party_person",
      "description": "Matches person names appearing after legal role indicators like 'klagenden Partei', 'beklagte Partei', 'gegen', 'Antragsteller', 'Antragsgegner'",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:klagenden Partei|beklagte Partei|gegen|Antragsteller|Antragsgegner|Vater|Mutter|Elternteil|Gesch\\u00e4ftsf\\u00fchrer|Pr\\u00e4sident|Mitglied)\\s+(?:der|die|des|dem)?\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 8,
      "reasoning": "Captures parties in legal proceedings. The pattern handles German articles (der/die/des/dem) and common role indicators. It stops at the first non-name character to avoid capturing company names or addresses."
    },
    {
      "name": "criminal_person",
      "description": "Matches person names in criminal cases after 'Strafsache gegen'",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Strafsache gegen)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 7,
      "reasoning": "Specifically targets criminal defendants mentioned after 'Strafsache gegen' which is a common pattern in the training data."
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": []
}

{
  "analysis": "The primary failure is that the 'title_person' rule incorrectly captures only the name part (e.g., 'Grohmann') instead of the full entity including the title (e.g., 'Dr. Grohmann'). This is due to the regex capturing only the name group ($1) while the output template uses $1, but the start/end offsets are calculated relative to the full match in some contexts or the capture group logic is flawed in the extraction. Additionally, the rule fails to handle complex titles like 'Univ.-Prof. Dr.', 'Hon.-Prof. PD Dr.', and 'MMag.' correctly, often stopping early or matching partial strings. There are also failures in detecting names without titles (e.g., 'Andreas Homrich', 'Johann Heisel').",
  "strategy": "1. Fix 'title_person' to capture the full title+name string using a single capture group for the entire name entity. 2. Add specific patterns for complex academic titles (Univ.-Prof., Hon.-Prof., PD Dr., MMag., Mag. Dr.). 3. Add a new rule 'standalone_person' to catch names appearing in contexts like 'wurde [Name] freigesprochen' or 'durch [Name] vertreten' where no title is present.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "title_person",
      "description": "Matches person names preceded by academic or professional titles (Dr., Mag., Univ.-Prof., Hon.-Prof., PhD, etc.), capturing the full title and name.",
      "format": "regex",
      "content": "(?:Dr\\.|Mag\\.|Univ\\.-Prof\\.|Hon\\.-Prof\\.|PhD|Vizepr\\.|Senatspr\\.|Hofrat|Hofr\\u00e4t|Prof\\.?)\\s+(?:[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+MBA)?(?:\\s+und\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "priority": 9,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities"
    },
    {
      "name": "complex_title_person",
      "description": "Matches person names with complex multi-part titles like 'Univ.-Prof. Dr.', 'Hon.-Prof. PD Dr.', 'MMag.', 'Mag. Dr.', 'DI', 'Ing.', 'Bakk. iur.'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "content": "(?:Univ\\.-Prof\\.\\s+Dr\\.|Hon\\.-Prof\\.\\s+PD\\s+Dr\\.|MMag\\.|Mag\\.\\s+Dr\\.|DI\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+|Ing\\.|Bakk\\.\\s+iur\\.\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+MBA)?(?:\\s+und\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*",
      "priority": 8,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$0",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities"
    },
    {
      "name": "standalone_person",
      "description": "Matches standalone person names in legal contexts where no title is present, e.g., after 'wurde', 'durch', 'gegen', or at the start of a sentence.",
      "format": "regex",
      "content": "(?:wurde|durch|gegen|als|von|mit)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "priority": 7,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities"
    },
    {
      "name": "party_person",
      "description": "Matches person names appearing after legal role indicators like 'klagenden Partei', 'beklagte Partei', 'Antragsteller', 'Antragsgegner'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "content": "(?:klagenden Partei|beklagte Partei|gegen|Antragsteller|Antragsgegner|Vater|Mutter|Elternteil|Gesch\\u00e4ftsf\\u00fchrer|Pr\\u00e4sident|Mitglied)\\s+(?:der|die|des|dem)?\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "priority": 6,
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities"
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": [
    "title_person",
    "party_person",
    "criminal_person"
  ]
}
